scenes.text: Srijan Shukla architected the pure domain core, the eleven-state deterministic finite state machine, and the tamper-evident cryptographic audit ledger.
Suhani Agarwal spearheaded the precision dual-clock SLA chronometer engine, business calendar arithmetic, and multi-tier escalation policies.
Kartikey Negi engineered the campus service dependency directed acyclic graph, Tarjan cycle validation, and major incident storm correlation.
Hairsh Kumar crafted the full-stack responsive interface, interactive Three.js hardware telemetry, and enterprise REST controller adapters.
Our platform adheres strictly to Ports and Adapters, or Hexagonal Architecture, isolating pure business entities completely from frameworks, persistence, and external drivers.
Eleven discrete domain modules are governed by Spring Modulith, running atop high-throughput Java 22 virtual threads and cloud-native PostgreSQL.
The frontend combines modern React 19 and Tailwind CSS with a distinctive 16-bit pixel-arcade design language, making operational monitoring engaging and intuitive.
Bi-directional Server-Sent Events stream live status updates across all connected stations, ensuring that student reports and technician actions remain synchronized with zero polling.
To guarantee long-term maintainability, the codebase enforces nine automated ArchUnit architectural rules that run on every compilation pass.

We now demonstrate Core Workflow 1, following an incident through all eleven finite states from initial report to cryptographic sealing.
Student Aarav Sharma logs into the self-service portal to report a critical failure on the SWD Mess and Fee Payment Gateway.
The student specifies high impact and high urgency. Our automated Priority Engine evaluates the campus calendar and notes an active fee payment window.
Because the service carries the FEE_DEADLINE calendar tag, the priority calculation automatically bumps the ticket to P1 Critical.

code_data.title: Priority Calculation Enum & Bands

scenes.text: A full priority explanation JSON array is embedded into the ticket, explaining the exact formula, calendar modifiers, and institutional rules applied.

code_data.title: Priority Explanation Audit Record

scenes.text: The ticket is routed via the Least-Loaded Strategy to Senior Technician Vikram Rao, moving state to ASSIGNED and starting the response clock.
Vikram clicks Acknowledge in the workbench. The initial response clock stops in two minutes, well under the five-minute P1 threshold.
Remediating the payment gateway, Vikram applies a database pool restart and enters detailed resolution notes exceeding the mandatory twenty-character validation.
The incident enters RESOLVED. Aarav receives a real-time notification, tests payment access, and confirms resolution with a five-star rating.
Finally, the IT Administrator archives the verified ticket into CLOSED status, immutably sealing its resolution record in the audit ledger.

scenes.text: Accountability requires unalterable proof. Incident-Zero guarantees non-repudiation through a cryptographically linked audit ledger.
Every ticket change computes a SHA-256 digest over the sequence index, timestamp, actor ID, action name, payload, and the prior hash.

code_data.title: SHA-256 Merkle Ledger Hash Engine

scenes.text: The admin console displays the unbroken cryptographic hash chain for every ticket, allowing one-click verification of history.
At the database level, an append-only trigger immediately rejects any UPDATE, DELETE, or TRUNCATE statement on audit records.

code_data.title: Immutable Audit Ledger Table DDL
code_data.code:
CREATE TABLE audit_record (
  id bigserial PRIMARY KEY,
  incident_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES incident (id),
  chain_index integer NOT NULL,
  ts timestamptz NOT NULL,
  actor_id uuid,
  actor_type text NOT NULL CHECK (actor_type IN ('USER','SYSTEM','AI','MCP')),
  action text NOT NULL,
  prev_state text,
  new_state text,
  description text NOT NULL,
  payload jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
  prev_hash char(64) NOT NULL,
  hash char(64) NOT NULL,
  UNIQUE (incident_id, chain_index)
);

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION audit_immutable() RETURNS trigger AS $$
BEGIN RAISE EXCEPTION 'audit_record is append-only'; END;
$$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;

CREATE TRIGGER audit_no_change BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE OR TRUNCATE ON audit_record
  FOR EACH STATEMENT EXECUTE FUNCTION audit_immutable();

CREATE TABLE sla_timer (
  id bigserial PRIMARY KEY,
  incident_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES incident (id),
  kind text NOT NULL CHECK (kind IN (
    'RESP_WARN_50','RESP_WARN_75','RESP_WARN_90','RESP_BREACH',
    'RES_WARN_50','RES_WARN_75','RES_WARN_90','RES_BREACH',
    'ESC_L2','ESC_L3','ESC_L4','AUTO_VERIFY_72H','USER_REMIND_24H'
  )),
  generation integer NOT NULL,
  due_at timestamptz NOT NULL,
  fired_at timestamptz,
